rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes increasing coherent phase boundary density via processing changes, while the target varies modulation period to create different interface types (coherent, semicoherent, grain-boundary-dominated). Both involve modifying interfaces, but the specific lever (modulation period vs. processing) and the type of interface targeted (coherent vs. semicoherent) differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies constant-load creep at service temperature, whereas the target uses room-temperature nanoindentation creep with varying loading rates. Both involve creep testing, but the loading mode, temperature, and specific conditions are different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes dislocation pinning at coherent phase boundaries to reduce creep, while the target proposes that semicoherent interfaces promote interfacial amorphization and diffusion/interface-slip creep. Both involve interface-mediated creep resistance, but the specific mechanism (pinning vs. amorphization) and the type of interface (coherent vs. semicoherent) are contradictory.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced creep rate with more coherent boundaries, while the target finds the best creep resistance with semicoherent interfaces (M16) and a transition to diffusion creep. Both predict improved creep resistance relative to a baseline, but the direction of the effect with respect to interface type is opposite.
